filter.searchPlaceholder: Type at least 3 letters to search

help.p1: This report shows antimicrobial use and the infection control review process, from the follow-up of each admission (courses, conformity evaluations, reviews and pending reasons).
help.p2: Each number counts by the date of its own record: days of therapy by the day, evaluations by the date they were recorded, courses by their start and admissions by the date their follow-up closed.
help.p3: Hover the icon next to each indicator to see how it is calculated.

conformity.title: Conformity
conformity.description: Evaluations, the record of the prescribed antimicrobials, non-conformity reasons, substitutions, interventions and evaluations by substance
conformity.withRecordHelp: Antimicrobial days (DOT) with an evaluation in force on the day, conforming or non-conforming ÷ DOT of the period. Days not evaluated (no evaluation or an expired one) count only in the total. It is the total of the Prescribed antimicrobials by record chart.
conformity.conformingHelp: Evaluations recorded in the period with a conforming verdict ÷ evaluations recorded in the period.
conformity.d3Help: Courses started in the period with an evaluation recorded by the end of treatment day 3 (72 hours) ÷ courses started. Courses still running that have not reached D3 are left out.
conformity.admissionsNonConformingHelp: Admissions with at least one non-conforming evaluation recorded in the period.

dotLot.title: DOT/LOT
dotLot.description: Days of therapy and days on antimicrobials of the period, and DOT by AWaRe classification, route and substance
dotLot.dotHelp: Sum, for each antimicrobial of each patient, of the calendar days it was prescribed in the period. Two antimicrobials on the same day count 2. Days the course was interrupted do not count.
dotLot.dotPer1000Help: DOT ÷ patient-days of the period × 1,000. Patient-days come from the Patient-Days report, with the same department and segment filters.
dotLot.lotHelp: Calendar days the patient received at least one antimicrobial, summed across patients. Unlike DOT, a day counts once regardless of how many antimicrobials.
dotLot.dotLotHelp: DOT ÷ LOT: how many antimicrobials, on average, per treatment day. 1.0 is monotherapy; higher values mean combinations.
dotLot.awareMixTarget: The WHO recommends at least 60% of DOT from the Access group.
dotLot.bySubstanceHelp: The 20 substances with the most days of therapy in the period, colored by AWaRe group.
dotLot.routeHelp: Share of the days of therapy by route. Intravenous follows the hospital's route mapping.
dotLot.useTrend: DOT and LOT per 1,000 patient-days by month
dotLot.useTrendHelp: For each month, DOT and LOT ÷ patient-days of the month × 1,000, and DOT ÷ LOT (right axis). Patient-days come from the Patient-Days report, with the same department and segment filters; a month without patient-days has no rate.
dotLot.awareTrendHelp: Share of each month's DOT in each WHO AWaRe group. The dashed line marks the 60% target of the Access group, at the bottom of each bar.

registry.title: Prescribed antimicrobials by record
registry.help: Antimicrobial days (DOT) of each month or day by the evaluation in force on the day: conforming, non-conforming or not evaluated (no evaluation or an expired one). Each bar is the period's DOT; hover to see the % of each.

departments.title: By department
departments.conformityDescription: Each number by the department of its own record: antimicrobial days by the department of the day, courses by the starting department, evaluations by the patient's department at the evaluation and admissions by the department at closing
departments.dotLotDescription: DOT, LOT and patients by the department of the antimicrobial day (a patient who stayed in more than one department counts in each); patient-days from the Patient-Days report
departments.reviewsDescription: Each admission by its department at closing, or the current one if still followed. Closed, % reviewed and the reviews count only the admissions closed in the period

drill.title: Admissions: {{department}}
drill.description: Admissions closed in the period or still followed that ended in this department, the same counted in the Admissions column. Click an admission to see its antimicrobials.
drill.noCourses: No antimicrobial recorded for this admission

process.title: Reviews
process.description: Review coverage and frequency, time to first review, pending reasons and reviewers
process.reviewedHelp: Admissions closed in the period with at least one review ÷ admissions closed in the period.
process.reviewsPerAdmissionHelp: Average reviews recorded per admission closed in the period. A review is each time the reviewer saves the patient's review, with one or more evaluations.
process.reviewsPer100DotHelp: Reviews of the closed admissions ÷ DOT of those admissions × 100. Adjusts the review frequency for treatment time.
process.firstReviewHelp: Hours between the start of the admission's follow-up and its first review. Shows the median across admissions; p90 is the time within which 90% were reviewed.
process.firstReviewBinsHelp: Admissions closed in the period by the time between the start of the follow-up and the first review.
process.pendingsHelp: Pending reasons opened in the period by type: how many are still open, the median hours to resolution and the share resolved by the team (evaluation, review or dismissal) rather than by the course ending or discharge.
process.reviewersHelp: Evaluations recorded in the period by reviewer, how many admissions they evaluated and the share of their evaluations with a non-conforming verdict.

appropriateness.reasonsHelp: Reasons of the non-conforming evaluations recorded in the period. An evaluation may have more than one reason.
appropriateness.bySubstanceHelp: Evaluations recorded in the period by substance and the share with a conforming verdict.
appropriateness.substitutionsHelp: Antimicrobial → substitute pairs recommended in the non-conforming evaluations of the period.
appropriateness.interventionsHelp: Interventions recorded from the evaluations of the period, by status, and the median hours between recording and outcome.

consumption.title: Consumption
consumption.description: Course length, route switch, restarts and combinations
consumption.courseLengthHelp: Treatment days of the finished courses (interruptions not counted); shows the median.
consumption.courseLengthBinsHelp: Finished courses by length in treatment days.
consumption.pastPlannedHelp: Finished courses that went past the length planned in the prescription ÷ finished courses with a planned length.
consumption.ivToOralHelp: Finished courses that started intravenous and switched to oral ÷ finished courses with a known starting route.
consumption.ivToOralDay: Day of the switch to oral
consumption.ivToOralDayHelp: Treatment day on which the course switched from intravenous to oral; shows the median.
consumption.restartHelp: Finished courses of an antimicrobial the patient had already received in an earlier course of the same admission (prescribed again after more than 36 hours without it) ÷ finished courses.
consumption.episodesHelp: Average antimicrobial episodes per closed admission. A new episode starts after more than 36 hours without any antimicrobial.
consumption.maxSimultaneousHelp: Closed admissions by the highest number of antimicrobials prescribed at the same time.

microbiology.title: Microbiology
microbiology.description: Cultures around the start of the courses and resistance results
microbiology.collectedBeforeHelp: Courses with a culture collected between 48 hours before and 24 hours after the start ÷ courses with cultures checked.
microbiology.positiveHelp: Positive cultures ÷ cultures collected during the follow-up.
microbiology.collectedHelp: Cultures collected during the follow-up of the admissions of the period.
microbiology.resistant: Resistance with the antimicrobial in use
microbiology.resistantHelp: Courses with a resistant result to the antimicrobial released while it was still in use ÷ courses with cultures checked.
microbiology.microorganismsHelp: Microorganisms identified in the cultures and in how many admissions they appeared (the 20 most frequent).

outcomes.title: Patient profile
